question.text: Suresh is evaluating two companies. Company A pays its instrument-holders from residual profits after external liabilities and tax, and its instruments are not backed by company assets. Company B's instrument-holders are paid an amount treated as an expense before computing taxable profits, and the instruments are usually secured against company assets. Which instruments do Company A and Company B represent respectively?

answer.text: Company A: Debentures, Company B: Preference shares
Company A: Preference shares, Company B: Debentures
Company A: Equity shares, Company B: Preference shares
Company A: Debentures, Company B: Equity shares

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series II-A (p.29), preference dividends are paid out of residual profits after external liabilities and tax, while debenture coupon interest is treated as an expense before calculating taxable profits, and debentures are usually secured on company assets. Per p.17, debt instruments carry an interest obligation and may be secured or unsecured; per p.24, equity capital does not have collateral security. Company A's facts match preference shares (post-tax dividend, no security) and Company B's facts match debentures (pre-tax interest expense, usually secured). The Trap: Option A reverses the two instruments. Options C and D bring in equity, which does not match the "fixed payment from residual profits" or "pre-tax expense" descriptions used in the stem. Note: The two diagnostic markers in the stem — tax treatment of the payout and whether the instrument is secured — together separate preference shares from debentures cleanly.
